cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Hello. Children’s Engineering Workshops.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Oh hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays.

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Sure.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: I have two daughters who are interested. The younger one’s Lydia, she’s four - do you take children as young as that?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Yes, our Tiny Engineers workshop is for four to five-year-olds.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: What sorts of activities do they do?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: All sorts. For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg (Q1), so that when it’s inside they can drop it from a height and it doesn’t break. Well, sometimes it does break but that’s part of the fun!

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Is there any opportunity for her to do that?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower (Q2). You’d be amazed how high they can go.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: But they’re learning all the time as well as having fun. For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car (Q3) that’s attached to a balloon, and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along. They go really fast too.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: OK, well, all this sounds perfect.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Now Carly, that’s my older daughter, has just had her seventh birthday, so presumably she’d be in a different group?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Yes, she’d be in the Junior Engineers. That’s for children from six to eight.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: And do they do the same sorts of activities?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Some are the same, but a bit more advanced. So they work out how to build model vehicles, things like cars and trucks, but also how to construct animals (Q4) using the same sorts of material and technique, and then they learn how they can program them and make them move.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: So they learn a bit of coding?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: They do. They pick it up really quickly. We’re there to help if they need it, but they learn from one another too.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Right. And do they have competition too?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Yes, with the Junior Engineers, it’s to use recycled materials like card and wood to build a bridge (Q5), and the longest one gets a prize.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: That sounds fun. I wouldn’t mind doing that myself!

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Then they have something a bit different, which is to think up an idea for a five-minute movie (Q6) and then film it, using special animation software. You’d be amazed what they come up with.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: And of course, that’s something they can put on their phone and take home to show all their friends.

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Exactly. And then they also build a robot in the shape of a human, and they decorate (Q7) it and program it so that it can move its arms and legs.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Perfect. So, is it the same price as the Tiny Engineers?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: It’s just a bit more: £50 for the five weeks.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: And are the classes on a Monday, too?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: They used to be, but we found it didn’t give our staff enough time to clear up after the first workshop, so we moved them to Wednesdays (Q8). The classes are held in the morning from ten to eleven.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: OK. That’s better for me actually. And what about the location? Where exactly are the workshops held?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: They’re in building 10A - there’s a big sign on the door, you can’t miss it, and that’s in Fradstone (Q9) Industrial Estate.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: Sorry?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Fradstone - that’s F-R-A-D-S-T-O-N-E.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: And that’s in Grasford, isn’t it?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: Yes, up past the station.

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: And will I have any parking (Q10) problems there?

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: No, there’s always plenty available. So would you like to enrol Lydia and Carly now?

cues.speaker: FATHER
cues.text: OK.

cues.speaker: SARAH
cues.text: So can I have your full name …
